meta.title: Speech Reach
meta.framing: Everything we look at here is already public. We track rules that change how far that speech travels in X’s For You feed — not whether it can be posted or read.
meta.privacyCore: We never publish individual account names or specific posts on this page. Full lists stay in the original public sources. This page only tracks public, code-visible limits on how speech is recommended in the feed.
methodology: The main source for each entry is the public open-source filter in the xai-org/x-algorithm repository (and any official dataset the filter cites).
Account counts come from the published code (for example, the Brazil filter’s own test checks list size).
Outcome metrics use the same kind of public sampling we use elsewhere on Elenchos for topics and signals.
All metrics are system-level totals only. We do not publish handles, user IDs, or individual posts here.
If you need the exact list of accounts, open the original public GitHub source (and official TSE open data where cited).
limitations: This is not a full map of every kind of content moderation on X.
This is not a national opinion poll or election forecast.
Reach and volume numbers are approximate directions — not a full count of the entire feed.
What you see in For You can still vary by who you follow, where you are, and product tests; we only report system-level patterns.
Paid boosting exceptions noted in the code comments are outside this first measurement window.
meta.futureNote: Speech Reach can add more country-specific recommendation rules as they show up in the public code, with the same privacy-safe approach — no individual accounts or posts on public pages.

entries.title: Brazil 2026 Election Recommendation Filter
entries.whatItDoes: Campaign accounts on Brazil’s election list are kept out of For You recommendations unless you already follow them. Their profiles and posts stay fully public and readable.
simpleWords: Anyone can still find and read their posts.
What changed: X will no longer automatically show those posts to people who do not already follow them.
whoIsOnList: These are roughly 665 official candidate and campaign accounts that registered their X profiles with Brazil’s Electoral Court (TSE) for the 2026 elections.
The list includes accounts from the full political spectrum — left, center, right, and smaller parties.
The rule applies equally to all of them. It is not aimed at one ideology.
Exact names remain only in the original public sources (link below).
entries.scaleLabel: About 665 campaign accounts on the public list
entries.activationNote: Live in X’s For You system for the Brazil 2026 elections. The chart’s “activation” mark is approximate to when the public code and announcement appeared.

spectrum.label: Left / progressive lists
spectrum.note: High-level groups only — not individual names

caveats: All figures are approximate directions, not exact census counts.
This is not a ranking of countries or a “censorship scoreboard.”
The activation mark on the chart is approximate.
Political spectrum buckets are rough groups for reading ease — not official TSE labels.

observations.text: Campaign messages reach existing followers more than new people in For You. Profiles and posts are still easy to open via follow, search, profile, or a direct link.
In our samples, more of the public conversation about major candidacies is coming from accounts that are not on the list — including ordinary users.
The same recommendation rule applies across the political spectrum for every account on the public list — not only one party or ideology.

The filter does not delete posts or close accounts. It only limits automatic For You recommendations for people who do not already follow those accounts (including some retweet, quote, and reply cases as written in the public code).

doesNot: Delete posts or hide profiles from the open web
Suspend or permanently remove accounts by itself
Block following, searching, or opening a profile directly
Publish or rank individual speakers on this page
